cards.text: The writer of this letter just warned his readers to test every spirit, because false prophets are out there (1 John 4:1). Now he switches gears, like a manager who wraps up the fire drill speech and goes, 'Okay, who wants cookies?' He says, 'Beloved, let us love one another,' and he's got a reason ready.

cards.question: The writer says, Let us love one another, because love comes from ___.

cards.text: Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God. That's a family resemblance, friend, like every cookie off my stamp coming out wearing my MUSTACHE.

cards.question: The writer says someone who doesn't love can still know God just fine. True or false?

cards.text: And here's why: 'God is love.' Three words, friend. My recipe cards need three PAGES just to say 'preheat the oven.'

cards.question: The writer says God's love was revealed among us. How did God show it?

answers.text: He sent His one and only Son into the world
He sent a prophet into every single nation
He wrote His law on two tablets of stone

cards.question: God sent His Son into the world so that we might ___ through Him.

cards.text: Then he tells us what love actually consists in. Big question, friend. I've been trying to explain the perfect cookie for YEARS and I still just point at the oven.

cards.question: So what does the writer say love consists in?

answers.text: God loved us and sent His Son
We kept every rule God gave us
We felt close to God every day

cards.question: The writer says God sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our ___.

cards.text: Calling them 'Beloved' again, he brings it home: if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. You get loved like THAT, friend, you don't sit on it like a cookie box nobody's allowed to open.
Then he drops a hard truth: no one has ever seen God. So how is anybody supposed to tell He's around?

cards.question: No one has ever seen God. But the writer says that if we love one another, God remains in us and His love is perfected in us. True or false?

cards.text: Next he tackles a big one: how do we KNOW we remain in God, and He in us? Friend, I spent years in a drawer stuffed with old receipts, and not ONE of them could've proved that.

cards.question: How does the writer say we know we remain in God and He in us?

answers.text: He has given us of His Spirit
We have never once doubted Him
We were raised in a godly home

cards.text: Then he says we have seen it and we testify: the Father sent His Son to be the Savior of the world. That's not a rumor from somebody's group chat, friend, that's EYEWITNESSES.

cards.question: The writer says that if anyone confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. True or false?

cards.text: He says we have come to know and believe the love God has for us. And then that line again: God is love. That's twice now, and I get it, friend. When I find a line I like, I say it so much my oven timer starts finishing my sentences.

cards.question: The writer says whoever abides in ___ abides in God, and God in him.

cards.text: He says love has been perfected among us, and it matters for the day of judgment. I hear 'judgment day' and I start holding my breath like I did every time somebody yanked open that junk drawer.

cards.question: The writer says love is perfected among us so that we may have ___ on the day of judgment.
What reason does the writer give for that confidence on the day of judgment?

answers.text: In this world we are just like Him
In this world we have done no wrong
In this world we have kept His law

cards.text: Then he says there is no fear in love. Friend, after all those years in a dark drawer, fear and I were on a first-name basis.

cards.question: What does the writer say perfect love does with fear?
The writer gives a reason perfect love drives out fear: fear involves punishment. True or false?

cards.text: So the one who fears has not been perfected in love. Then he says it plain: 'We love because He first loved us.'
Now somebody says, 'I love God,' but hates his brother. That's like me in that junk drawer, swearing I LOVE every gadget on earth while I won't say one word to the twist tie lying right next to me.

cards.question: What does the writer call someone who says he loves God but hates his brother?
The writer says a person can love God, whom he hasn't seen, without loving his brother, whom he has seen. True or false?
The writer says whoever loves God must love his brother as well. What does he call that?

findings.problem: The opening setup only says that the writer has a reason ready. It gives no basis for inferring whether love comes from God, ourselves or effort, so the blank asks for wording the baker has not seen rather than a meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about God being love, the observation that it is three words and the recipe-card joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The earlier cards establish only that God sent His Son into the world. They give no context from which to infer His purpose, so choosing live rather than rule or rest is a guess at the unseen wording.
